article_ref: SI 2011/1881, regs. 15 (declaration & marking duty) and 18 (marking placement)
title: United Kingdom: toy safety, marking and declaration
summary: A toy placed on the GB market requires conformity assessment against the essential safety requirements, a declaration of conformity, and UKCA or CE marking. Flagged in v1; category depth is v2.

required_evidence.label: Test evidence against the applicable toy safety standards

sources.title: The Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/1881)
sources.note: Fetched the statute directly. Reg. 15 requires the manufacturer to draw up a declaration of conformity and affix the UK marking per reg. 18 once conformity assessment demonstrates the toy meets the essential safety requirements; reg. 18 sets the placement rules (visible/legible/indelible, on the toy/label/packaging, with a small-toy carve-out). Continued CE-marking recognition for GB is confirmed current via the same primary source used for uk.marking.ukca-or-ce in this batch (SI 2024/696) -- no separate citation needed here since that row already covers it and this row's applies_when doesn't duplicate the marking-choice logic. DATE FIX: effective_from was 2011-07-20 (the EU Directive's date, drafted 'by analogy'); this SI's own commencement (reg. 1(2)) is 19 August 2011 -- a month later. Corrected to 2011-08-19.
